div.p: Russian-born translator and writer. Living in Paris during and after the WWI years and writing for several literary reviews, she met Ezra Pound, who convinced her to translate into French JJ’s A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man. In 1920, she and her husband Marcel Bloch offered their flat in Paris to the newly-arrived JJ and his family for several months and, through French poet André Spire, hosted a soirée for JJ to be introduced to the Parisian literary world. Despite some antagonism between author and translator, Dedalus: Portrait de l'artiste jeune par lui-même (Paris: Éditions de la Sirène) was published in 1924; it remained for decades the work’s standard French translation. In 1948, her translation of JJ’s Stephen le Héros (Paris: Gallimard) appeared. She subsequently translated into French works by John Rodker, Virginia Woolf, Christopher Isherwood, and Ivy Compton-Burnett. William Brockman
